sections.explanation: A vector has magnitude and direction; a scalar has magnitude without direction. Add and subtract vectors component by component. For (x,y), magnitude is √(x²+y²). A vector of magnitude r at angleθ has components (r cosθ,r sinθ). Unit vectors have magnitude1; divide a non-zero vector by its magnitude to obtain its direction unit vector. The zero vector has no unique direction. Use atan2(y,x), rather than arctan(y/x), to preserve quadrant information.
sections.worked: For a=(3,4) and b=(−1,2), a+b=(2,6), a−b=(4,2), and |a|=5. The unit direction of a is(3/5,4/5). A displacement magnitude is not the sum of component magnitudes.
tasks: Explain why(−1,1) and(1,−1) cannot have the same direction despite equal y/x.
feedback: They lie in different quadrants; the ratio alone loses that information.
